reason: Every load-bearing claim reproduces. Source: lately.html:485 `.rise { animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) both; }` with :480 `to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }`; the KPI cards carry it (:693 `<a class="kpi rise">`), and :323/:325 are exactly `a.kpi:hover { border-color: var(--line); transform: translateY(-2px); }` / `a.kpi:active { transform: translateY(0); }`. A forwards-filling animation sits in the animation origin and outranks a plain author declaration, so transform on a.kpi is pinned. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 with real pointer travel into the card centre and a held mouse-down, in all three motion modes (settled default, ?motion=play, prefers-reduced-motion), computed transform on a.kpi read matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0) at rest, on hover and on press, identically; el.getAnimations() reported rise:finished:both on the card in every mode. The only surviving hover channel is border-color rgba(17,17,17,0.055) to rgba(17,17,17,0.1) (#f2f2f2 to #e7e7e7 composited on white) - a 1px hairline going from about 4% to 7% ink. On press, transform, background-color and border-color were byte-identical to hover, so the press has no channel at all; :325's translateY(0) is the rest value anyway, so it could not have paid even if the pin were lifted. The gate reading is right too: interaction-check.mjs proves 'every control acknowledges a press' by string-matching 'a.kpi:active' in document.styleSheets (`has(sel)` over cssRules), so it passes on a rule that has never painted - L-06 exactly. This is the same mechanism the file's own comment at :290 records ('a clip-path keyframe with fill:both outranks any plain author declaration') and that record-tag-never-paints closed in r1, returned on the one interactive region on the screen; it is evidence of a live recurrence, not a re-raise of no-pressed-state-anywhere, because it proves the r1 rule is decoration. Severity defect is right, not higher: focus-visible still paints, the cards still read, and nothing on screen asserts something untrue - it is an interactive affordance that is present in the source and absent on the glass. The proposed fix was patched into the served master (via route interception, lab untouched) and measured: with the animationend listener at :1151 plus the widened :active, hover read matrix(1,0,0,1,0,-2) and press read background rgb(244,244,245) / border rgb(161,161,170) in all three modes, and all eleven .rise classes were released with no jump; both halves of the fix land, and both tokens are already in the lock and already used by .btn:hover (:438). Confirmed.
sharpenedFix: The seat's fix works as measured, but it buys with JS what one CSS word buys outright. Prefer: at lately.html:485 change `.rise { animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) both; ... }` to `... backwards; ...`. rise's `to` frame (opacity 1, transform none) is byte-identical to the element's natural resting state, so dropping only the forwards half changes no pixel of the entrance, keeps the backwards half that hides the element during its stagger delay, and releases transform back to the author cascade the instant the run ends. Measured in the same harness: hover matrix(1,0,0,1,0,-2), press background rgb(244,244,245), border rgb(161,161,170), identical in settled, play and reduced-motion, with the class still on all eleven elements. It needs no per-render wiring, and it cannot be defeated by a descendant's animationend bubbling into a `{ once: true }` listener and consuming it before the element's own event arrives - a hazard the seat's version only escapes by timing luck (.record-tag at :290 runs a keyframe literally named `rise` inside .card.hero.rise, and only its 1.5s delay keeps it from racing the hero's own 565ms end). Keep the second half of the seat's fix verbatim: replace :325 with `a.kpi:active { transform: translateY(0); background: var(--paper-3); border-color: var(--ink-4); }`. Then close the gate hole that let this through: interaction-check.mjs must stop proving the press by string-matching 'a.kpi:active' in document.styleSheets and instead hover the card with a real pointer, hold mouse-down, and assert that the computed transform/background/border triple differs from rest AND from hover - otherwise the identical class of bug re-enters on the next control.
breaks: Small blast radius, three things to re-measure. (1) `backwards` un-pins transform, opacity and everything else rise's `to` frame was silently holding on all eleven .rise elements, not just the KPIs - re-shoot all ten frames and diff, particularly light-loading (where `[data-state="loading"] * { animation: none !important }` already removes the pin, so nothing should move) and light-first-run. (2) The press adds a background the `.kpi` transition does not list (:319 covers border-color and transform only), so background snaps in and out with no ease; that is right for a press, but if it reads harsh, add `background-color 0.14s var(--ease)` to the same transition rather than reaching for a new token. Re-run audit.mjs: the audit measures contrast against the real composited backdrop, and the pressed card puts ink #111 and the dim-2 secondary line on --paper-3 #f4f4f5 instead of #ffffff - .btn:hover already ships that exact pair and passes, so it should hold, but it is the one measurement that could newly fail. (3) The dark ground swaps --paper-3 to #27272a and --ink-4 to #71717a; check the pressed card against .kpi.lead's neighbour so the press does not read as the lead card's fill. If the seat's animationend variant is taken instead of `backwards`, it must stay after the skeleton fix-ups at :1144-1151 - the loading state replaces `.sk-wrap a`/`button` with fresh spans, and listeners attached earlier are discarded with the originals - and no future CSS or gate may select `.rise` as a hook, since the class stops existing about 600ms in (nothing does today: neither audit.mjs nor interaction-check.mjs matches it).
